_comment: SQ-5 residual-vulnerability allow-list. Each entry is a transitive advisory with NO upstream patch available at the time of writing. New/patchable vulnerabilities are NOT allowed here — fix them by pinning a patched version (see PCI.Backend.csproj). Every entry must carry a reason, a residual-risk assessment, and a review_by date. Governed by docs/testing/SUPPRESSION_PROCESS.md.

allow.reason: Memory-corruption defect in the native SQLite library bundled by SQLitePCLRaw. The advisory covers all versions <= 2.1.11 with NO patched release available upstream as of 2026-07 (we already pin the newest available, 2.1.11, which supersedes the transitive 2.1.6).
allow.residual_risk: Exploitation requires an attacker to run attacker-controlled SQL (a crafted statement with a very large number of aggregate terms). The PCI backend issues only parameterised, developer-authored SQL and never executes user-supplied SQL text, so the vulnerable code path is not reachable from any request surface. Production additionally runs on MySQL (dual-provider), where this native SQLite library is not loaded at all. Risk is assessed LOW in our deployment.
allow.action_when_patched: Remove this entry and bump the SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlite3 pin (or Microsoft.Data.Sqlite) to the first patched version; the gate will then block again if it ever regresses.
